   141→- **Perf issue.** A measured slowness to trace and improve against a baseline.
   142→- **Hillclimb.** Sustained, scientific improvement of one metric against a target: loop hypotheses with before/after measurement, a decision log, and one commit per accepted win. Distinct from Perf issue, which is a one-off fix.

     1→# `$init` delivery entry point
     2→
     3→`$init JUL-nnn` has one implementation: `initCommand` in
     4→`ops/mastra-agents/reviewer/src/mastra/cli.ts`. The former
     5→`scripts/julia-init.mjs` selection wrapper was a second implementation and has
     6→been removed.
     7→
     8→On Todd's Windows laptop, commands that need Julia vault secrets go through the
     9→restricted service-account helper:
    10→
    11→```powershell
    12→.\scripts\julia-vault-windows.ps1 -JuliaArguments @('$init', 'JUL-225')
    13→.\scripts\julia-vault-windows.ps1 -JuliaArguments @('$init', 'JUL-225', 'Start')
    14→.\scripts\julia-vault-windows.ps1 -JuliaArguments @('$init', 'JUL-225', 'Cancel')
    15→```
    16→
    17→The first command reads the Linear card and displays the saved four-role model
    18→choices and accepted limits. `Start` requires matching start authorization,
    19→validated tested connections, current model offers, and a complete Ready card;
    20→it saves the immutable run snapshot before delivery. `Cancel` does not dispatch.
    21→A resumed run uses its saved snapshot rather than rereading role defaults.
    22→
    23→Do not invoke a second script-level `$init`, and do not use personal 1Password
    24→desktop authentication for commands that need Julia secrets.
    25→
    26→## Local initialization control page
    27→
    28→Double-click `Start Julia Control Page.cmd` to open
    29→`http://127.0.0.1:43123/julia-control`. The launcher uses the restricted Julia
    30→vault helper, and the server binds only to loopback. The page discovers current
    31→Ready cards and current model offers without reading `role-defaults.json`.
    32→
    33→The loopback bind stays. To reach the same page from another device in the
    34→tailnet, the operator fronts it with Tailscale Serve (never Funnel) and sets
    35→`JULIA_CONTROL_TAILSCALE_HOST` to this host's own tailnet DNS name (for example
    36→`JULIA_CONTROL_TAILSCALE_HOST=ovh.<tailnet>.ts.net`; a comma-separated list is
    37→accepted). Serve terminates TLS for that name and proxies to the loopback
    38→listener, so a request arriving with the server's own name as its Host came
    39→through Serve. The boundary continues to refuse every other Host, including
    40→other tailnet names; leaving the variable unset keeps the page loopback-only.
    41→
    42→Start creates or reuses one file-backed Mastra workflow run suspended at
    43→`ready-for-build`; it does not execute a delivery role. Cancel removes the form
    44→in the browser and sends no request. Close the launcher's window to stop the
    45→local server. This control page is not a Factory route.
    46→
    47→The same loopback server exposes `GET /julia-control/api/runs` as a read-only
    48→validated machine boundary. It returns the complete initialized-run collection,
    49→the independently computed total count, and structured activity counts. It has

- **explorer** (explorer): Complete the assigned pstack role.
- **architect-a** (architect-a): Complete the assigned pstack role.
- **architect-b** (architect-b): Complete the assigned pstack role.
- **coder** (coder): Complete the assigned pstack role.
- **reviewer** (reviewer): Complete the assigned pstack role.

By default the subagent runs in its own context — it does NOT see the parent conversation history. Write a clear, self-contained task description.

Set `forked: true` for context-dependent parallel work that needs the parent conversation, prior tool results, or the parent tool environment. Omit it for self-contained delegation. A forked subagent reuses the parent agent's instructions and tools so the prompt prefix stays cache-friendly.

Use this tool when:
- You want to run multiple investigations in parallel
- The task is self-contained and can be delegated

task.description: Clear, self-contained description of what the subagent should do. For non-forked subagents include all relevant context — the subagent cannot see the parent conversation.

modelId.description: Optional model ID override for this task. Ignored when `forked: true` (the parent agent's model is used).

forked.description: If true, fork the parent conversation: clone the parent thread and run with the parent agent's instructions/tools so prompt cache is preserved. Requires memory to be configured on the AgentController. Defaults to the subagent definition's `forked` setting.

function.name: mastra_workspace_read_file
function.description: Read a file from the workspace filesystem. Text files come back as text — use offset/limit to read a line range from large files. Supported media files come back as a native file part you can view directly. Other binary files return only their metadata (path, size, mime type) since their raw contents are not useful to read.

path.description: The path to the file to read (e.g., "data/config.json")

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed). Only used when reading text files; ignored for media and other binary files. Defaults to line 1 if omitted.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read. Only used when reading text files; ignored for media and other binary files. Defaults to the end of the file if omitted.

showLineNumbers.description: Prefix each line with its line number. Only used when reading text files; ignored for media and other binary files. Defaults to true if omitted.

encoding.description: Usually omit this — text files and supported media are handled automatically. Pass `base64` or `hex` to get the file's raw bytes encoded as text when you need to inspect an unsupported binary file that would otherwise only return metadata (e.g. checking a file header or magic bytes).

function.name: mastra_workspace_edit_file
function.description:
Edit a file by replacing specific text. The old_string must match exactly and be unique in the file.

Usage:
- Read the file first to get the exact text to replace.
- By default, read file output includes line number prefixes (e.g., "     1→"). Ensure you preserve the exact indentation as it appears AFTER the arrow. Never include any part of the line number prefix in old_string or new_string.
- Include enough surrounding context (multiple lines) to make old_string unique. If it still isn't unique, include more lines.
- Use replace_all only when intentionally replacing all occurrences.

path.description: The path to the file to edit

old_string.description: The exact text to find and replace. Must be unique in the file.

new_string.description: The text to replace old_string with

replace_all.description: If true, replace all occurrences. If false (default), old_string must be unique.

function.name: execute_command
function.description:
Execute a shell command in the workspace sandbox.

Examples:
  "npm install && npm run build"
  "ls -la src/"
  "cat config.json | jq '.database'"
  "cd /app && python main.py"

Usage:
- Commands run in a shell, so pipes, redirects, and chaining (&&, ||, ;) all work.
- Always quote file paths that contain spaces (e.g., cd "/path/with spaces").
- Use the timeout parameter (in seconds) to limit execution time. Behavior when omitted depends on the sandbox provider.
- Optionally use cwd to override the working directory. Commands run from the sandbox's configured workingDirectory (or the provider default) if omitted.

Set background: true to run long-running commands (dev servers, watchers) without blocking. You'll get a PID to track the process.

command.description: The shell command to execute (e.g., "npm install", "ls -la src/", "cat file.txt | grep error")

timeout.description: Maximum execution time in seconds. Example: 60 for 1 minute.

tail.description: For foreground commands: limit output to the last N lines, similar to tail -n. Defaults to 200. Use 0 for no limit.

background.description: Run the command in the background. Returns a PID immediately instead of waiting for completion. Use get_process_output to check on it later.

function.name: mastra_workspace_get_process_output
function.description:
Get the current output (stdout, stderr) and status of a background process by its PID.

Use this after starting a background command with execute_command (background: true) to check if the process is still running and read its output.

pid.description: The process ID returned when the background command was started

tail.description: Number of lines to return, similar to tail -n. Positive or negative returns last N lines from end. Defaults to 200. Use 0 for no limit.

wait.description: If true, block until the process exits and return the final output. Useful for short-lived background commands where you want to wait for the result.

function.name: mastra_workspace_kill_process
function.description:
Kill a background process by its PID.

Use this to stop a long-running background process that was started with execute_command (background: true). Returns the last 50 lines of output.

pid.description: The process ID of the background process to kill
